hints.title: Two Pass Frequency Separation
hints.text: Characters in the string may repeat at earlier or later positions. Can an initial pass tally character frequencies so that a second pass immediately identifies the first non-repeating element?

hints.title: Bounded Alphabet Size Invariant
hints.text: Because the alphabet consists solely of lowercase English letters, frequencies can be tracked across at most twenty-six distinct characters.

hints.title: Count And Search Index Procedure
hints.text: Iterate through the string once to count each character frequency. Then iterate through the string a second time, checking the recorded frequency of each character at its original index. Return the first index whose frequency equals one, or return negative one if none exists.

hints.title: See the blueprint

complexity.notes: Optimal solution achieving O(N) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Comparing each character against every other character results in an O(N^2) quadratic nested loop.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Counting character frequencies in a fixed 26-element array takes O(N) time and O(1) space because the alphabet size is constant.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should recognize that a 26-bucket array qualifies as constant O(1) space and articulate the clean two-pass structure.
